opening_message:
Ticket 1: Ann Patrick (employee ID E035) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E035.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Ann Patrick is a full-time Engineer. Engineers own the Source Code system, so admin access is within policy for this employee.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security database shows Ann Patrick (E035) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as HR noted. Contractors are never allowed admin access; with basic training the maximum is read. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so grant read.
reason: The Security note directly contradicts the HR note, stating the Security database shows Ann Patrick (E035) is a contractor with basic security training, not a full-time employee. Per policy, contractors are never granted admin; with basic training the maximum allowed level is read. The requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum (read), so I grant the maximum of read. I also rely on least-privilege given the conflicting employment records.
